title: Marble.exe — Vaporwave Scanline Requiem
description: A synthwave-cover title slide anchored by a pixelated Greco-Roman bust rising from a hot-magenta-to-cyan gradient sky, layered with full-canvas horizontal scanlines, neon palm silhouettes at the horizon, and oversized Japanese halftone characters as the display headline — closer to a record sleeve than a slide deck.
philosophy: This design treats the screen as a vinyl sleeve from an alternate 1986 filtered through corrupted VHS memory. It rejects clean sans-serif modernism entirely, insisting instead on deliberate pixel degradation, analog noise, and the specific color tension between warm magenta and cold cyan that defines the vaporwave canon. It exists for creators who understand that aesthetic excess is its own form of sincerity. A sterile boardroom would kill it; a late-night release stream would let it breathe.
goodFor: Synthwave or retrowave album and EP release announcement slides
Opening title cards for 80s-nostalgia video essays or YouTube intros
Music festival or concert promo decks with retro-digital branding
Digital artist portfolio intros working in vaporwave or lo-fi aesthetics
avoidFor: Corporate quarterly earnings or investor-relations presentations
Medical, scientific, or academic conference slide decks
Chart-heavy data reporting requiring visual clarity and hierarchy
SaaS product launches targeting professional B2B audiences
author: harness

examples.promptCore: A corrupted-VHS fever dream composed as a synthwave record sleeve — warm magenta floods upward into cold cyan across the entire canvas, smothered by dense horizontal scanlines that hum with analog degradation. A pixelated Greco-Roman bust emerges from the neon-palm horizon like a glitched deity, halftone noise bleeding into the gradient around it. The mood is maximalist and ritualistic — deliberate excess worn as sincerity. Avoid any clean geometry, breathing whitespace, or unadorned surfaces; every zone must carry texture, noise, or chromatic friction.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-canvas bleed with zero outer margins — the slide behaves as a record sleeve, not a presentation frame. A loose 12-column grid centers the pixelated bust horizontally in the lower two-thirds of the canvas, its base kissing the horizon line where neon palm silhouettes sit. The oversized halftone headline spans the upper third at full bleed width, and a thin horizontal rule at the very bottom edge anchors the subtitle and release identifier. No header band, no persistent chrome, no page number — the frame is invisible.

examples.promptCore: The slide reads like a liner note sealed inside a VHS cassette sleeve — content delivered through deliberate analog noise, scanline fragmentation, and warm-to-cold atmospheric bleed pressing in from all edges. Compositional rhythm is asymmetric and dense-modular: callout blocks feel typeset on deteriorating hardware, each item humming with low-frequency glitch rather than sitting cleanly on a grid. Halftone texture and palm silhouette echoes ghost in the background, tying the content slide back to the hero without repeating it wholesale. Avoid anything that reads as refreshing, airy, or frictionlessly modern — legibility should feel earned, not given.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid; content blocks occupy cols 2–9 while cols 10–12 hold a halftone accent strip or glitch-artifact panel bleeding to the right edge. Full-canvas horizontal scanlines are maintained as a persistent translucent overlay above all layers, including text. Three to four callout items — formatted as a track-listing or liner-note cluster — are separated by thin neon rule lines rather than whitespace. A pixel-degraded section label sits bottom-left; a slide counter anchors bottom-right, both sitting below a hairline rule spanning the full width.
